title: Ministry of External Affairs India Foreigner Registration (FRRO) and e-Visa Framework
source: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
content:
All foreign nationals entering India on long-term visas exceeding 180 days (such as Employment, Student, Research, or Medical visas) are required to register with the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO) or Foreigners Registration Officer (FRO) within 14 days of arrival.

Registration is conducted electronically via the e-FRRO portal without requiring a physical visit unless summoned. Required documentation includes a valid passport, visa, proof of residence in India (Form C submitted by the landlord or hotel), employment contract (for Employment Visa holders), and recent passport-sized photographs.

Foreign nationals holding Tourist Visas or short-term Business Visas valid up to 180 days are generally exempt from registration unless their continuous stay exceeds 180 days. A Residential Permit is issued electronically upon successful verification of submitted documents.

title: Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) Aadhaar Guidelines for Resident Foreigners
publisher: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India
content:
A foreign national who has resided in India for a period or periods amounting to 182 days or more in the 12 months immediately preceding the date of application is eligible to apply for an Aadhaar number under the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016.

Aadhaar is a 12-digit unique identity number that serves as proof of identity and proof of address across India, facilitating local banking, telecommunication SIM cards, and domestic regulatory services.

Aadhaar is not proof of citizenship or domicile. Resident foreign nationals must submit their valid passport, valid long-term visa or OCI card, Form C or registered lease agreement as proof of address, and undergo biometric capture (fingerprints and iris scans) at an authorized Aadhaar Enrolment Centre.

title: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Regulations on Banking and Digital UPI for Foreign Nationals
content:
Foreign nationals relocating to India for employment or study are permitted to open Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) accounts or resident bank accounts depending on their tax residency status under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).

Upon obtaining an Indian mobile number and opening an Indian bank account, foreign residents are fully eligible to utilize the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) for instant peer-to-peer and merchant digital payments across the country.

Additionally, international inbound travellers and delegates from select countries can access UPI One World prepaid wallets issued at authorized international airports and exchange points, enabling seamless QR code-based digital transactions at registered merchants.

title: Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) Municipal Services and Property Registration in Mumbai
content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), also known as the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), governs public health, municipal water supply, road maintenance, and civic services across Mumbai's 24 administrative wards.

Residential tenancy agreements in Mumbai must be registered under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999, via the Department of Registration and Stamps (e-Registration system). Tenancies typically follow an 11-month Leave and License format with a refundable security deposit.

Police verification of tenants is mandatory across all Mumbai Police commissionerate zones before occupancy. The BMC provides online birth/death registration, property tax payments, and emergency disaster helplines via its centralized citizen portal.

title: Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Public Transport Operations and Metro Smart Card
content:
The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation operates a mass rapid transit network spanning over 390 kilometers and 12 operational lines (including the Airport Express Line) connecting the National Capital Territory of Delhi with Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad, Gurugram, and Faridabad.

Commuters use contactless Smart Cards offering a 10% discount on base fares, or digital QR tickets via the official DMRC Travel mobile application. National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) debit/credit cards are accepted on all AFC gates.

Fares range from 10 INR for short trips to 60 INR for maximum network journeys. Metro trains operate daily from approximately 05:30 to 23:30, with peak frequencies ranging between 2 and 4 minutes on high-density corridors like the Yellow and Blue lines.
